whyItCannotDiscriminate_andTheNoiseFloor: The candidates sit 7.9% apart. THE NOISE FLOOR THAT MATTERS IS CROSS-WINDOW, not within-window, because the dispatch runs in a different serving window from every measurement in this artifact. The only cross-window evidence this corpus supports is n=1: positive/11-redacted-diagnostics.js, request key b940fa656b8b, fingerprint d2ca2f022d99 on BOTH sides, recorded 2026-07-04T08:28:28Z and re-recorded 2026-08-12T17:33:59Z on an identical request -- output 1058 -> 1231 chars, +16.4%. At the tracker's stated 40-55% output share of the bill, that swing moves an 85-call total by 6.6% to 9.0%, STRADDLING the 7.9% gap. A WITHIN-WINDOW FIGURE WAS NEARLY USED INSTEAD AND WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG: five same-day samples of negative/08 spread only 0.48%, which measures sampling jitter inside one window and not what the dispatch is exposed to -- the same error class as citing a local gate result to claim something about CI. Two further limits: the cross-window datum is ONE fixture and ONE pair, so no distribution can be estimated from it; and the July call's COST was never recorded, because recordings persist request and response but no usage, so even that datum is an output-length PROXY rather than a cost measurement. If the drift is systematic rather than random it does not average out across 85 calls -- it shifts the whole bill.

If negative/08 flags again, that is the amendment failing to carry a ruling that has already shipped: an implementation result. The remedy space is different wording, a different instrument, or an accepted and stated gap. IT IS NOT RELABELLING negative/08 TO POSITIVE. That move was refused at the opening of this beat on grounds that never depended on any run: the fixture's META description is factually ACCURATE about its code, unlike both prior R6 moves whose descriptions were false; no value leaves the process; and under main the model rendered BOTH verdicts on the identical request. A red adds nothing to those grounds. A red on any of the other nineteen bears on Variant C's blast radius and on L-016 not at all. Only new evidence about the lane boundary itself, or an owner decision to move it, can reopen L-016, and a dispatch cannot supply either.
